result.topic_en: Riemann derives the integrability conditions (curvature equations) that the coefficients b of a quadratic differential form must satisfy if the form can be transformed into a sum of squares, and introduces the invariant curvature expression built from them.
result.transcription:
12.

$(6)\quad 2\frac{\partial^2 x_\nu}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}} = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial s_\iota}{\partial x_\nu} p_{\iota,\iota',\iota''}$.

Quantitatibus $p_{\iota,\iota',\iota''}$ iterum differentiatis obtinetur
$\frac{\partial p_{\iota,\iota',\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'''}} - \frac{\partial p_{\iota,\iota',\iota'''}}{\partial s_{\iota''}} = 2\sum\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_{\iota}\partial s_{\iota''}}\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota'''}} - 2\sum\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_{\iota}\partial s_{\iota'''}}\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}}$
unde tandem prodit, substitutis valoribus modo inventis e (6) et (4)
N.B. 2 vorg. [?] lassen.
$(I)\quad 2\left(\frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota,\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota',\iota'''}}{\partial s_{\iota}\partial s_{\iota''}} - \qquad\right) + \qquad = 0$
Hujusmodi igitur aequationibus functiones $b$ satisfaciant necesse est, quando $\sum_{\iota,\iota'} b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in formam $\sum_\iota dx_\iota^2$ transformari potest; partes laevas harum aequationum designabimus per
$(\iota\iota',\iota''\iota''')$.

Ut indoles harum aequationum melius perspiciatur, formetur expressio
$\delta\delta\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'} - 2d\delta\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} + dd\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\delta s_\iota\delta s_{\iota'}$
determinatis variationibus secundi ordinis $d^2$, $d\delta$, $\delta^2$ ita, ut sit


denotante $\delta'$ variationem quamcunque. Quo pacto haec expressio invenietur
N.B. $\Sigma$ über alle Paare $\iota\iota'$, und alle Paare $\iota''\iota'''$ $\iota<\iota'$, $\iota''<\iota'''$.
$(II)\quad = \sum(\iota\iota',\iota''\iota''')(ds_\iota\delta s_{\iota'} - ds_{\iota'}\delta s_\iota)(ds_{\iota''}\delta s_{\iota'''} - ds_{\iota'''}\delta s_{\iota''})$
Jam ex hac formatione hujus expressionis sponte patet, mutatis variabilibus independentibus transmutari eam in expressionem a nova forma ipsius $\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ eadem lege dependentem. At si quantitates $b$ sunt constantes, omnes coefficientes expressionis (II) cifrae [-ae-]aequales evadunt. Unde si $\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in expressionem similem constantibus coefficientibus affectam transformari potest, expressio II identice evanescat necesse est.

Perinde patet, si expressio II non evanescat,
N.B. mit $-1$ mul. [?] tiplicirt.
$(III)\quad \frac{\frac{1}{2}\sum(\iota\iota',\iota''\iota''')}{\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\delta s_\iota\delta s_{\iota'} - (\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota\delta s_{\iota'})^2}$
mutatis variabilibus independentibus non mutari insuperque immutatam

methods.what: Necessary conditions (vanishing of the Riemann curvature tensor) for a quadratic form to be transformable to a sum of squares
methods.quote: $(I)\quad 2\left(\frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota,\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota',\iota'''}}{\partial s_{\iota}\partial s_{\iota''}} - \qquad\right) + \qquad = 0$

methods.what: Second-variation construction yielding the invariant quadrilinear curvature form

items.quote: Hujusmodi igitur aequationibus functiones $b$ satisfaciant necesse est, quando $\sum_{\iota,\iota'} b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in formam $\sum_\iota dx_\iota^2$ transformari potest
items.english: The functions b must therefore satisfy equations of this kind when the form can be transformed into the form sum dx^2.

items.quote: Jam ex hac formatione hujus expressionis sponte patet, mutatis variabilibus independentibus transmutari eam in expressionem a nova forma ipsius $\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ eadem lege dependentem.
items.english: From this construction it is evident that, when the independent variables are changed, the expression is transformed into an expression depending by the same law on the new form of the quadratic form.

items.quote: Unde si $\sum b_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in expressionem similem constantibus coefficientibus affectam transformari potest, expressio II identice evanescat necesse est.
items.english: Hence if the form can be transformed into a similar expression with constant coefficients, expression II must vanish identically.

items.quote: Perinde patet, si expressio II non evanescat,
items.english: Likewise it is evident that if expression II does not vanish, (III) is not changed when the independent variables are changed, and moreover unchanged ...
